Q1 • Determine the fraction of the Sun's luminosity that is intercepted by the Earth. • What luminosity does this correspond to? [주어진 값] L⊙ = 3.85 × 10³³ erg s⁻¹, R⊙ = 6.96 × 10¹⁰ cm, au = 1.50 × 10¹³ cm, R⊕ = 6.37 × 10⁸ cm
A1 • The fraction of the Sun's luminosity that is intercepted by the Earth is f = πR⊕² / (4π (au)²) = 4.5 × 10⁻¹⁰
• The intercepted luminosity is L_int = f L⊙ = 1.73 × 10²⁴ erg s⁻¹
• The total primary power consumption on Earth is approximately 2 × 10²⁰ erg s⁻¹.
Q2 • What is the astrophysical flux of the Sun?
• What is the (frequency-integrated) intensity of the Sun?
• What is the solar constant, which is the flux of the Sun at a distance of 1au?
A2 • Astrophysical flux of the Sun F⊙ = L⊙ / (4πR⊙²) = 6.33 × 10¹⁰ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻²
• Using F = πI, I⊙ = F⊙/π = 2 × 10¹⁰ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² sr⁻¹
• Solar constant is S⊙ = L⊙ / (4π (au)²) = 1.367 × 10⁶ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² = 1.367 × 10³ W m⁻²
Q3 [그림: Cas A 두 장 — (a) 붉은/노란 색의 전파(radio) 영상, (b) 광학·X선 합성 영상] • Cas A is an SNR. It is located 3.4 kpc away and has a linear diameter of 4 pc. What is the solid angle subtended by Cas A?
A3 • Cas A subtends a linear angle, θ = d/D = 4/3.4e3 = 1.18 × 10⁻³ rad
• For an ellipse on the sky of angular major axis and minor axis diameters of θ₁ and θ₂, respectively, the two-dimensional solid angle, in steradians, is Ω = πθ₁θ₂/4. Thus, Ω = 1.09 × 10⁻⁶ sr

Q4 • Cas A has L_radio = 3 × 10³⁵ erg s⁻¹ in the radio band. Assuming that Cas A has a spectral luminosity between ν₁ = 10⁷ Hz and ν₂ = 2 × 10¹⁰ Hz of the form, L_ν = K ν^−0.7, where K is a constant, determine the value of K and specify its units. Also find L_ν and L_λ at ν = 1900 MHz.
A4 • Units: L_ν = K ν^−0.7 ; erg s⁻¹ Hz⁻¹ = [K] Hz^−0.7 ➔ [K] = erg s⁻¹ Hz^−0.3
• The value of K: L_radio = ∫_{ν1}^{ν2} L_ν dν = ∫_{ν1}^{ν2} K ν^−0.7 dν = 3 × 10³⁵ erg s⁻¹ ➔ K = 8.36 × 10³¹ erg s⁻¹ Hz^−0.3
• L_ν and L_λ at ν = 1900 MHz: L_ν = Kν^−0.7 = 2.67 × 10²⁵ erg s⁻¹ Hz⁻¹ ; L_λ = L_ν |dν/dλ| = (ν²/c) L_ν = 3.22 × 10³³ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻¹

Q5 • Determine the flux density (in Jy = 10⁻²³ erg cm⁻² s⁻¹ Hz⁻¹) of a cell phone that emits 2 mW cm⁻² at a frequency of 1900 MHz over a bandwidth of 30 kHz (assume a flat spectrum) and of the Sun, as measured at the Earth, at the same frequency.
• Compare these to the flux density of Cas A, which is the strongest radio source in the sky after the Sun.
• Comment on the potential of cell phones to interfere with the detection of astronomical signals.
A5 • Flux from the cell phone is f_ν^c = 2 × 10⁻³ W cm⁻² = 2 × 10⁴ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻². – Assuming a flat spectrum, the flux density is f_ν(cell) = f(cell)/Δν = 0.67 erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² Hz⁻¹ = 6.7 × 10²² Jy
• From the Sun, by adopting T_eff = 5800 K, B_ν^S = 2ν²kT/c² = 6.42 × 10⁻¹⁵ erg cm⁻² Hz⁻¹ sr⁻¹. The flux density at the Earth will be f_ν^S = B_ν^S πθ⊙²/4 = 4.36 × 10⁴ Jy
• The flux density of Cas A is f_ν^CasA = L_ν/(4πD²) = 1.93 × 10³ Jy

• It is quite clear that the cell phone signal will swamp the brightest radio emitter (the Sun) as well as the brightest nighttime radio emitter (Cas A), and therefore every other radio source in the sky at this frequency.
